deferrals.evidence: forensics/tools/atlas_runtime.py parse_option_list()/_OPTION_ROW and _OPTION_VALTYPES (repaired by 22.9; the row's original citations :240/:243 have moved with the rewrite); forensics/atlas/phase22/cli-surface.json (22.9's structured surface: 120 commands -- 54 standard, 1 deprecated, 18 digest aliases, 47 cipher aliases -- with 4,314 structured options, 0 refused rows and 0 commands with zero options); RT-PHASE22-CLI in artifacts/phase22/COURTS.json (proves the repaired parser reads a real row, refuses a malformed one, and fails when broken in memory); forensics/atlas/openssl-3.6.4-production/cli-commands.json still records command_count 55 and option_count 0 on all 55 commands, because it has not been regenerated
deferrals.reason: Transferred to 22.9 and repaired there; what remains deferred to Phase 16 is regenerating the Phase-1 capture with the fixed parser. parse_option_list() (forensics/tools/atlas_runtime.py) matched the authority's `openssl list -options <cmd>` rows against a help-text shape (`-in val        Input file`) that the output never produces, and the real rows are `name type` pairs (`help -`, `in <`, `provider s`) with no leading indent, no leading dash and no description column, so every structured option_count was 0 and all 2,008 raw rows stayed unstructured. 22.9 rewrote the parser to the authority's actual grammar and re-enumerated the whole namespace from the authority's own built binary (forensics/authorities/build/openssl-3.6.4-production/apps/openssl): forensics/atlas/phase22/cli-surface.json now carries 120 commands with 4,314 structured options, 0 refused rows and 0 commands_with_zero_options, and RT-PHASE22-CLI proves the repaired parser reads a real row and refuses a malformed one (and turns to fail when the parser is broken in memory). The Phase-16-owned Phase-1 capture forensics/atlas/openssl-3.6.4-production/cli-commands.json still carries option_count 0 on all 55 commands: it is Phase 16 (cli-config) that owns the CLI stratum and would regenerate production and historical in lockstep, since regenerating only the production authority would leave a spurious option-set differential against the historical one. Closure: parse_option_list() reads the authority's actual option shape and the structured surface (22.9's cli-surface.json now, and the Phase-16 capture once regenerated) has a non-zero structured option_count for every command.

body.note: `open` is the only list that blocks this stratum, and its count is over provider registration rows, prerequisite deferrals and contract units rather than exported symbols, so the `implemented` and `open` *export* lists are empty by measurement and `open_in_this_stratum` is the live count. A provider row is a registration row, not an export: the provider-row rule in `phase_state.py` and the provider-row census remain the arbiter of its state, and `handed on` is the census's `projection`, not a state a row carries (D237, D295). The 39 legacy rows belong to the loadable module the candidate ships as a scaffold `ossl-modules/legacy.so`, which Phase 13's subphases do not activate and which this stratum owns as the installed-module contract (D525). The six prerequisite deferrals are the `OPENSSLDIR` directory plane, the install context, the absent dynamic ENGINE loader (D528) and the CLI capture defect (D490), plus the two TLS message-layer units Phase 15 sealed without. Nothing here is a parity claim: a published provider row or a landed CLI is at most `IMPLEMENTED` in docs/PARITY_MODEL.md terms, and docs/PHASE-16-SUBPHASES.md section 4 decides when the stratum may be called complete.

unit_deferrals.reason: Phase 14.5b's plan row names this unit to say the client half of the TLS message layer remains unlanded: the state machine's control surface and a fresh-connection driver (`statem.c`) landed, but the client message construction and parsing (`statem_clnt.c`) did not, so no flight is built or parsed on the client side and no court reads one. Phase 14 deferred the unit to Phase 15 (QUIC/ECH), whose plan section 0 names the QUIC object the method table points at; but Phase 15's landed scope is the three `quic.h` constructors and its plan excludes the message layer, so Phase 15 seals without it (docs/PHASE-15-QUIC-SEAL.md) and the deferral is corrected here to Phase 16, the next later stratum in `phase_state.py`'s `REQUIRES` DAG. The owner is named rather than left implicit, the disposition D132 established.
